question: If a coil of a conductor with 50 Ω resistance is subjected to time varying magnetic field such that the EMF induced is 5 V, then the induced current in the coil is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1 A.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **induced current **in the coil is given by **Ohm's law,** which states that** I = V/R, **where V is the induced EMF and R is the resistance of the coil.
 
• Thus, the induced current in the coil is** 5/50 = 0.1 A.**
 
• The **direction** of the induced current is determined by **Lenz's law,** which states that the direction of the induced current is such that it** opposes **the **change in magnetic flux **that caused it.
 
• In this case, the **time varying magnetic field** is inducing an** EMF **in the coil, so the induced current will flow in a direction that** creates a magnetic field** that opposes the original magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **coil** of conductor is a device that consists of a **series of loops of wire.**
 
• When a **magnetic field** passes through the coil, it induces an **EMF in the coil**, which can cause a** current to flow** if the coil is connected to a circuit.
 
• The** resistance **of the coil is a measure of how much the** coil resists the flow of current **through it.
 
• It depends on the **material of the wire, **the **length and cross-sectional area** of the wire, and the **temperature **of the wire.
